To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) the logit scores of a network can be used to predict the performance of that network on unseen data and 2) the logit score can be used to regularize the network during training.

(1) the problem of over-fitting and lack of adaptivity is caused by the tendency of the network weights to become large; (2) the solution is to use a weight normalization technique that is designed to keep weights in a small, finite range; and (3) we have developed such a technique, called Logit Attenuating (LA) Weight Normalization, which has been shown to be effective in improving generalization performance of over-parameterized deep networks in both image classification and text

1) the logit attenuation phenomenon is caused by a mismatch between the gradient and the weight space, and 2) the logit attenuating weight normalization (LAWN) technique can be used to alleviate this mismatch, and thus, the logit attenuation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: 1) Why does over-parameterization cause large logit and weight values? and 2) How can we fix this? We show that over-parameterization causes large logit and weights due to the fact that the network is not able to escape the region of low train loss.
improving the generalization performance of over-parameterized deep networks by reducing the tendency of the network to produce large logits and weights.
the problem of training deep networks using adaptive optimizers, with an aim to improve their generalization performance, especially in the image classification problem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for deep networks, adaptive optimizers are not as good as SGD in generalization performance, and that this is mainly due to the fact that adaptive optimizers are more aggressive than SGD at minimizing training loss.
adaptive optimizers are not as good as SGD for image classification, and that the main reason is that they do not have the same level of adaptivity as SGD.

the adaptive optimizers like Adam and Adagrad have a tendency to overfit the training set and underfit the test set, while the SGD based optimizers like RMSProp, Adadelta, and Adamax have a tendency to underfit the training set but overfit the test set.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel method of weight normalization, called Logit Attenuation Weight Normalization (LAWN).

we propose a simple yet effective way of regularizing the network weights, that is complementary to the standard WD, and is applicable to any deep network trained using SGD, momentum-SGD, and adaptive optimizers.
we have proposed an alternative to weight decay that works well with adaptive optimizers and improves their generalization performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we show that, with a simple and elegant modification to weight normalization (called Logit Attenuating weight normalization or LAWN) that is orthogonal to WD, adaptive optimizers like Adam can be made to perform as well as or better than SGD.
the logit values and the network weights should be normalized together, and not independently.
, by simply scaling down the weight norm at the output of every layer, we can achieve better generalization with adaptive optimizers, without having to sacrifice training performance.
